title: When to Take Maternity Photos: A Rio Grande Valley Guide
description: When to take maternity photos? Many families choose about 28–34 weeks. Here’s how to time your McAllen-area studio session and save a newborn spot, too.
h1: When to take maternity photos: finding your sweet spot
dek: A calm, practical guide to timing your maternity portraits — the weeks many families choose, when to go a little earlier, and how to line up your newborn session in the same step.
intro:
As general guidance, many families take maternity photos between about 28 and 34 weeks of pregnancy. By then the bump is clearly visible, and moving around, standing and posing are usually still comfortable.

That window is a guide, not a deadline. If you’re deciding when to take maternity photos for your own pregnancy, this guide walks through why those weeks work so well and when going a little earlier makes sense. We’ll also cover what a studio session in the McAllen area is like, and how to save a spot for your newborn session at the same time — wherever in the Rio Grande Valley you call home.

sections.h2: Why 28–34 weeks is a common sweet spot
sections.html:
When to do maternity photos really depends on two things: your bump and your energy. Before about 28 weeks, many bumps are still small enough to disappear under a soft dress or a flowing gown. Over the following weeks the curve becomes clear from almost every angle — and that shape is what makes a maternity portrait feel like one.

At the other end, the last weeks of pregnancy often bring swelling, broken sleep and a body that would much rather rest. Portraits ask a little of you — standing, turning, shifting your weight — so it helps to schedule them while that still feels easy.

A simple way to think about the window:

  • Around 28–30 weeks: a defined bump and, for many people, steady energy.
  • Around 31–34 weeks: a fuller, rounder bump. Choose the time of day you usually feel your best.
  • Past 34 weeks: still possible for many families who feel well. Book it soon rather than waiting for the perfect week.

There’s a practical bonus, too. After every session, we sit together and help you choose your favorite images, and your edited photos are delivered within one week — so portraits taken in this window are ready well before your due date.

sections.h2: When going a little earlier makes sense
sections.html:
If you’re deciding when to get maternity photos with twins on the way, it’s common to plan a little earlier — often near the start of that window or just before it. Twin bumps tend to show sooner, and many parents find the final stretch more tiring.

The same thinking applies if your doctor suggests resting more, or if this pregnancy has simply felt heavier than you expected. Your doctor knows your situation best, so check with them if you’re unsure, then choose a date that suits your body rather than a chart.

A few signs it may be time to book sooner rather than later:

  • You’re carrying twins (or more).
  • Your doctor has mentioned taking it easy.
  • Being on your feet for a while already leaves you worn out.
  • You feel wonderful right now — which is a perfectly good reason, too.

Above all, listen to your body. The right week for your photos is the one when you feel comfortable enough to enjoy them.

sections.h2: Why a studio session takes the pressure off
sections.html:
Maternity sessions with Adrisabel take place in her private studio in the McAllen area, so there’s no Valley heat or wind to plan around. You won’t be checking the forecast all week, waiting for a cooler weekend or fixing your hair between gusts.

That matters for timing more than you might think. Weather-dependent plans have a way of slipping, and a delay of a few weeks can carry you past the window you hoped for. In the studio, the weather simply isn’t part of the decision.

It’s easier on your partner, too. Nobody enjoys standing outside in a long dress or a buttoned-up shirt in the afternoon heat. Indoors, you can both relax and enjoy the time together — you’ll find more about the session itself on our maternity photography page.

Studio gowns are available, and Adrisabel helps you plan outfits and colors that feel like you, so there’s no need to shop for anything special. If you do want to wear something of your own, though, the calendar matters more than you might expect.

Your bump keeps growing between the day you buy an outfit and the day of your session, so stretchy or adjustable pieces are a safer bet than something that fits perfectly today. Try everything on again about a week before.

For partners and kids, settle the colors early and do a quick try-on the week of the session. Little ones have a way of outgrowing things overnight.

sections.h2: Bring your partner and the soon-to-be big siblings
sections.html:
Partners and big brothers and sisters are welcome. A maternity session can be about the whole family getting ready to grow: a hand resting on the bump, a toddler curious about the baby inside, everyone close together.

If children are joining, a little planning helps them enjoy it:

  • Pick a time of day when they’re usually rested and happy.
  • Feed them before you leave and pack a tidy snack for the car.
  • Talk about the baby on the way — kids who feel part of the day tend to lean in naturally.
  • Let them warm up at their own pace. A shy start is completely normal.

In a few weeks, today’s big brother may be the one leaning in to kiss the baby. Photographing both chapters — the waiting and the welcome — tells the whole story.

sections.h2: Reserve your newborn session at the same time
sections.html:
Booking maternity is the perfect time to reserve your newborn session too. Newborn portraits are best in the first 5–14 days after birth, while babies are sleepy and curl up easily, and those days arrive quickly.

Here’s how it works. We save a spot around your due date, and when your baby arrives, you send us a message and we set the session within that 5–14 day window. Early or late babies are completely normal — the session is simply set when your little one is here.

There are two newborn sessions to choose from:

  • Sunshine (baby only): 8 edited photos, 2 outfits and 2 backdrops.
  • Wonderland (baby, siblings and parents): 15 edited photos, 2 outfits and 4 backdrops.

Both are on our newborn photography page, and our guide on when to do newborn photos has more on timing that first session. Expecting twins? They can be added to any package, with 4 extra photos included.

sections.h2: Planning your drive to the studio
sections.html:
Families come to the studio from all over the Rio Grande Valley. From McAllen and Pharr it’s just minutes; Mission is about 10–20 minutes away, Edinburg about 15–20 minutes, Harlingen about 40–45 minutes and Brownsville about 60–70 minutes.

If you’re coming from farther out, choose a time that leaves room for traffic and a stop to stretch your legs — long car rides can feel longer in the third trimester. Bring water, and plan to arrive a few minutes early so you can settle in without rushing.

When you’re ready, ask about a maternity session through our booking form, or call or text (409) 354-3075. We reply within 24 hours with maternity details and availability, and we can save your newborn spot in the same conversation. Sessions are Monday through Saturday by appointment, and a 50% deposit via Zelle reserves your date.

faq.q: Is 35 weeks too late for maternity photos?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Many families aim for about 28–34 weeks, but how you feel matters more than the exact week, so follow your body and your doctor’s advice. If you’re already past that window, send us a message and we’ll talk through timing together.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book my maternity session?
faq.a: Reaching out early gives you the most choice of dates within your window, and the second trimester is a good time to do it. It’s also a natural moment to reserve your newborn session, so both can be planned around your due date.
